chapters.title: 3 John 1 — Hospitality, faithful partnership, and humble leadership
chapters.historicalContext: The elder writes personally to Gaius, commending his faithful hospitality toward travelling Christian workers. The letter contrasts Gaius' generosity with Diotrephes' desire for prominence and celebrates Demetrius' good testimony.
chapters.overview: John rejoices that Gaius walks in truth and supports workers who serve for the sake of Christ. He condemns the self-seeking conduct of Diotrephes and encourages the church to imitate what is good.
chapters.studyObservation: Hospitality becomes practical partnership in mission. The contrast between Gaius and Diotrephes shows how humility and the desire for control shape the health of a church.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read with 2 John, which balances hospitality with discernment, and Romans 12:9–13 on sincere love and hospitality. The commendation of Demetrius highlights the value of a trustworthy witness.
chapters.lifeApplication: Support faithful workers, practise generous hospitality, and resist leadership driven by pride or control. Build a reputation for truth and goodness.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: The brief account of Diotrephes should not be used to settle modern disputes without evidence. The principle concerns self-serving leadership and rejection of healthy accountability.
chapters.readingNote: Compare the three named examples—Gaius, Diotrephes, and Demetrius—and ask what each reveals about truth, hospitality, and leadership.
studyQuestions: How does Gaius demonstrate practical partnership in the gospel?
What makes Diotrephes' conduct harmful to the church?
Why does John connect a good testimony with doing what is good?
